g.text: Figure 1a · From prose to a requested view
Published narrative · Aesop, The Lion and the Mouse · exploratory extraction

text.style: font-weight: 700; font-size: 9px; font-family: 'Paper-figure_1a_fable_overview'; text-anchor: start; fill: #142d40
font-weight: 700; font-size: 8.5px; font-family: 'Paper-figure_1a_fable_overview'; text-anchor: start; fill: #315d82

g.text: A LION was awakened from sleep by a Mouse running over his face.

text.style: font-weight: 700; font-size: 8.5px; font-family: 'Paper-figure_1a_fable_overview'; text-anchor: start; fill: #315d82

g.text: Rising up angrily, he caught him and was about to kill him, when the Mouse piteously
entreated, saying: “If you would only spare my life, I would be sure to repay your

text.style: font-weight: 700; font-size: 8.5px; font-family: 'Paper-figure_1a_fable_overview'; text-anchor: start; fill: #315d82

g.text: The Lion laughed and let him go.

text.style: font-weight: 700; font-size: 8.5px; font-family: 'Paper-figure_1a_fable_overview'; text-anchor: start; fill: #315d82

g.text: It happened shortly after this that the Lion was caught by some hunters, who bound him
by strong ropes to the ground.

text.style: font-weight: 700; font-size: 8.5px; font-family: 'Paper-figure_1a_fable_overview'; text-anchor: start; fill: #315d82

g.text: The Mouse, recognizing his roar, came and gnawed the rope with his teeth, and set him

text.style: font-weight: 700; font-size: 8.5px; font-family: 'Paper-figure_1a_fable_overview'; text-anchor: start; fill: #315d82

g.text: “You ridiculed the idea of my ever being able to help you, not expecting to receive from
me any repayment of your favour; now you know that it is possible for even a Mouse to
